questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered a method of conservation of natural resources?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Extraction**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Extraction** is not considered a method of conservation of natural resources.
 
• Conservation methods typically include practices that help preserve and protect natural resources, such as **afforestation, recycling, and terrace farming**.
 
• **Afforestation** refers to planting trees to create forests, which helps in maintaining ecological balance.
 
• **Recycling** involves converting waste materials into reusable materials, thereby reducing the need for new raw materials.
 
• **Terrace farming** is an agricultural practice that prevents soil erosion and conserves water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Natural resource conservation** is essential for sustainable development and ensuring that resources are available for future generations.
 
• Methods such as **afforestation** and **recycling** help in reducing the environmental impact and preserving biodiversity.
 
• **Extraction**, on the other hand, often depletes natural resources and can cause significant environmental damage if not managed sustainably.
 
• Conservation efforts focus on sustainable practices to maintain the health of ecosystems and the availability of resources.

questions.question: Under which of the following Mughal emperors were the Marathas a major challenge to the sovereignty of the Mughals?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Marathas posed a significant challenge to the sovereignty of the Mughals during the reign of **Aurangzeb**.
 
• Aurangzeb's prolonged military campaigns in the Deccan region were largely aimed at subduing the Marathas.
 
• Despite his efforts, the Marathas continued to resist Mughal rule and expanded their influence, especially after the death of Aurangzeb.
 
• This period marked the rise of the Maratha Empire, which later became a dominant power in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• His reign is often considered the last effective Mughal rule, after which the empire began to decline.
 
• The Maratha leader, **Shivaji**, was a key figure in resisting Mughal dominance during Aurangzeb's reign.
 
• Aurangzeb's policies and military campaigns significantly strained the Mughal treasury and weakened the empire's central authority.
 
• The decline of the Mughal Empire post-Aurangzeb allowed regional powers like the Marathas to gain prominence.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a poverty alleviation programme in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Namami Gange**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Namami Gange** is NOT a poverty alleviation programme in India.
 
• Namami Gange is an integrated conservation mission, approved as the 'Flagship Programme' by the Union Government in June 2014 with a budget outlay of Rs. 20,000 Crore to accomplish the twin objectives of effective abatement of pollution, conservation, and rejuvenation of the National River Ganga.
 
• It focuses on activities such as sewage treatment infrastructure, river surface cleaning, rural sanitation, and afforestation.
 
• Other options like **Indira Awaas Yojana (IAY)**, **Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP)**, and **Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY)** are indeed poverty alleviation programmes aimed at improving living conditions and providing employment opportunities in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indira Awaas Yojana (IAY)** was a major scheme for constructing houses for the rural poor in India, which has now been subsumed under the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana (PMAY).
 
• **Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP)** aimed at generating employment opportunities in rural areas through the establishment of micro-enterprises.
 
• **Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY)** was launched to provide additional wage employment and food security in rural areas, along with the creation of durable community assets.
 
• The **Namami Gange Programme** focuses on the holistic rejuvenation of the Ganga river and does not directly address poverty alleviation.

questions.question: Using Fleming’s right-hand rule, in which direction will the current flow if the direction of magnetic field is towards north and the conductor is moving vertically upward?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Towards west**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Using **Fleming's right-hand rule**, if the direction of the magnetic field is towards north and the conductor is moving vertically upward, the current will flow towards the west.
 
• Fleming's right-hand rule states that if you extend the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of your right hand such that they are mutually perpendicular, with the thumb pointing in the direction of motion of the conductor, and the forefinger in the direction of the magnetic field, then the middle finger will point in the direction of the induced current.
 
• In this scenario, with the magnetic field towards the north and the conductor moving upward, the thumb points upward, the forefinger points north, and the middle finger points towards the west.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fleming's right-hand rule** is used to determine the direction of induced current in a conductor moving in a magnetic field.
 
• It is particularly useful in the context of generators and other devices where mechanical motion is converted into electrical energy.
 
• Conversely, **Fleming's left-hand rule** is used for electric motors where electrical energy is converted into mechanical motion.
 
• Both rules are fundamental principles in electromagnetism and are widely used in physics and engineering.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nucleolus – Synthesis of DNA**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nucleolus – Synthesis of DNA** is incorrectly matched. The nucleolus is primarily involved in the synthesis of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and the assembly of ribosomes, not DNA synthesis.
 
• The **mitochondria** are correctly matched with the production of chemical energy (ATP) through the process of cellular respiration.
 
• The **ribosome** is correctly involved in the assembly of proteins.
 
• The **nucleus** is correctly matched with the storage of genetic information in the form of DNA.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **nucleolus** is a substructure within the nucleus where ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is produced and combined with proteins to form ribosome subunits.
 
• The **mitochondria** are known as the powerhouses of the cell, converting nutrients into adenosine triphosphate (ATP), the cell's main energy currency.
 
• **Ribosomes** are the molecular machines in the cell that facilitate the translation of mRNA into proteins.
 
• The **nucleus** contains the cell's genetic material (DNA) and is responsible for controlling the cell's growth, metabolism, and reproduction.
 
• Understanding the correct functions of cellular components is essential for studying cell biology and related biomedical fields.

questions.question: The location of ‘Dhamek Stupa’ is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarnath**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dhamek Stupa** is located in **Sarnath**.
 
• Sarnath is a famous pilgrimage site for Buddhists and is located near Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• The stupa was built by the Mauryan emperor **Ashoka** in 249 BCE.
 
• It marks the spot where Buddha is said to have given his first sermon to his five disciples after attaining enlightenment, known as the **Dharmachakra Pravartana (Turning of the Wheel of Dharma)**.
 
• The Dhamek Stupa is one of the most visited and revered Buddhist structures in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The original stupa, commissioned by Ashoka, was a simple structure, but it was later expanded and embellished during the Gupta period.
 
• Sarnath also houses the remains of several other ancient structures, including monasteries and temples, which reflect the rich cultural and religious heritage of the site.
 
• Excavations at Sarnath have uncovered a wealth of artifacts, inscriptions, and sculptures that provide valuable insights into the history and development of Buddhism in India.
 
• The **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** manages the site and has undertaken extensive conservation efforts to preserve its historical and cultural significance.
 
• Sarnath is also home to the **Archaeological Museum**, which houses a remarkable collection of artifacts, including the famous **Lion Capital of Ashoka**, which is now the national emblem of India.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that there shall be a Supreme Court of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 124**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 124** of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a Supreme Court of India.
 
• The Supreme Court is the highest judicial court and the final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
 
• It has extensive powers in the form of original, appellate, and advisory jurisdictions.
 
• The Supreme Court also has the power to interpret the Constitution and has the authority for judicial review to ensure the protection of fundamental rights.
 
• The Chief Justice of India heads the Supreme Court, along with other judges as prescribed by Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Supreme Court** was established on January 28, 1950, two days after India became a Republic.
 
• It succeeded the Federal Court of India, which was established under the Government of India Act 1935.
 
• The Supreme Court has the power to transfer cases from one High Court to another and also from one subordinate court to another.
 
• It can also issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
• The judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President of India.
 
• The retirement age for Supreme Court judges is 65 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abdel Fattah Al Sisi** was the chief guest at India's 74th Republic Day parade.
 
• Abdel Fattah Al Sisi is the President of Egypt.
 
• India's Republic Day is celebrated on **26th January** every year to honor the date on which the Constitution of India came into effect in 1950.
 
• The Republic Day parade is a major attraction, showcasing India's military might, cultural diversity, and advancements.
 
• Inviting a foreign dignitary as the chief guest is a tradition to strengthen bilateral ties and showcase India's diplomatic relations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The tradition of having a chief guest from another country started with the first Republic Day in 1950.
 
• Over the years, various world leaders have graced the occasion, reflecting India's international relations.
 
• The Republic Day celebrations include a grand parade at Rajpath, New Delhi, which is attended by the President of India, the Prime Minister, and other dignitaries.
 
• The parade showcases India's defense capabilities, cultural heritage, and technological advancements through various tableaux and performances.
 
• The event is concluded with a flypast by the Indian Air Force, marking the strength and prowess of India's armed forces.

questions.question: Who among the following Kushana kings was the founder of the Kushana dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kujula Kadphises**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kujula Kadphises** was the founder of the Kushana dynasty.
 
• The Kushana dynasty played a significant role in the history of India and Central Asia, especially during the early centuries of the Common Era.
 
• Kujula Kadphises established the Kushana empire in the 1st century CE, which later expanded under his successors.
 
• Under the Kushana rule, there was significant cultural exchange and economic prosperity, with notable developments in art, architecture, and trade.
 
• The dynasty is known for its patronage of Buddhism and the spread of Buddhist culture along the Silk Road.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Kushana dynasty's most famous rulers include **Kanishka**, who is known for his military, political, and spiritual achievements.
 
• The Kushana empire facilitated the spread of Buddhism to Central Asia and China, significantly influencing the development of Mahayana Buddhism.
 
• The dynasty issued a large number of gold and copper coins, which provide valuable insights into their reign and the cultural syncretism of the period.
 
• The Kushana period is also notable for the development of the Gandhara and Mathura schools of art, which combined Indian, Persian, and Greek artistic traditions.
 
• The capital of the Kushana empire was initially in Bactria (modern-day Afghanistan) and later moved to Peshawar (in present-day Pakistan).
